erd.title: ERD (Effective Rim Diameter)
erd.description:
The diameter measured between the points where the spoke nipples seat on the rim — i.e., the effective circle the spoke ends form.

This is NOT the rim's outer or bead diameter. Most rim makers publish the ERD; if not, measure it with a ruler or dedicated ERD gauge.

Assumes 12 mm nipples.

Unit: mm.

rimOffset.title: Rim Offset
rimOffset.description:
The lateral displacement from the rim centre plane to the spoke holes (nipple seats).

Enter an unsigned offset amount. The calculator automatically applies it in the direction that reduces the difference between the effective left and right centre-to-flange distances. If both flange distances are equal, the offset does not affect the calculation.

If the entered offset is greater than the difference between the left and right flange distances, it increases the asymmetry compared with no offset, and a warning appears below the input.

Unit: mm.

pcd.title: PCD (Pitch Circle Diameter)
pcd.description:
The diameter of the circle passing through the centres of the spoke holes on the hub flange.

Left and Right flanges often have different PCDs (especially on rear hubs and disc-brake hubs), so measure each side separately.

Unit: mm.

flangeDistance.title: Flange Distance
flangeDistance.description:
The horizontal distance from the hub's centre plane (centreline of the locknuts) to each flange.

Left and Right are usually asymmetric due to cassette / disc rotor offset — measure each side independently.

Unit: mm.

spokeHoleDiameter.title: Spoke Hole Diameter
spokeHoleDiameter.description:
The diameter of the spoke holes on the hub flange. Used to correct the spoke length so the spoke reaches across the hole rather than its centre.

Typically around 2.5 mm for standard hubs.

Unit: mm.

crossings.title: Crossings
crossings.description:
The number of times each spoke crosses other spokes between the hub and the rim.

0 = radial (straight from hub to rim).
2 or 3 cross is most common; 4 cross is used on some high-load builds.

Left and Right can use different crossing counts.

about.title: About this app
about.body:
A web application for (as accurately as possible) calculating the spoke lengths required for bicycle wheel building. Lengths come from common formulas combining the cosine rule (planar) and Pythagoras' theorem (3D).

It assumes 12 mm nipples. If you want to be strictly accurate, you need to account for the rim's inner wall thickness and the nipple length, so please modify the tool if you care about those details.

Each parameter is based on what can be entered from the Hope Pro 5 specification document. If the calculations from this tool don't work out, please don't complain to the author — improve it yourself.

Most of the code in this project was created with Claude Code. It is distributed under the MIT License.

usage.title: How to use
usage.intro: Enter the rim and hub dimensions and the spoke lengths for both sides follow along.

input.title: Enter basic information
input.body:
Enter the rim and hub dimensions, then select the number of spokes and the lacing pattern.
To use a preset, the chip beside the "Input Values" heading fills a whole wheel, and the chips beside the Rim and Hub headings fill just that section.

result.title: Read the result
result.body: Spoke lengths for both sides update live as you type. There is no Calculate button.

save.title: Save results
save.body: Save a calculation under a name of your choice. Saved data can be recalled later.

share.title: Share the inputs
share.body:
"Share", in the action bar under the results, builds a URL carrying the current input conditions. Devices with a share sheet open it; elsewhere the link is copied to the clipboard.
Only the inputs travel in the URL — results and saved data do not.

compare.title: Compare wheels
compare.body:
"Compare", in the action bar, opens the comparison over the wheel you have and the one you want to build. Either side can be a preset, a saved calculation or the current inputs, so nothing has to be saved first.
The result is how many spokes can be reused, how many are left over, and what to buy for each side.

manage.title: Manage your data
manage.body: Export the calculation data as a JSON file and import it back. Saved data can also be deleted.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.empty: There are no changes recorded for this year.

v0_5_0.notes:
Number of Spokes and Crossings can now be set by sliding your finger across the options.
Holding down a stepper button in a number field now keeps changing the value.

v0_4_0.notes: The menu can now be closed by swiping it back the way it came in.

v0_3_0.notes:
Tapping a number field now shows stepper buttons inside it, so you can adjust a value without retyping it.
Pasting into a number field no longer wipes the value, and scrolling the wheel over a focused field no longer changes it.
The decimal point key now appears on phone keyboards, so decimals can be entered in any field.
The Japanese typeface is now M PLUS 2. It matches Sora used for Latin text, and loads less font data.
Closing a dialog on Android no longer leaves the page behind it scrolled out of place.

v0_2_1.notes:
The results bar now follows your browser's font size settings, like the rest of the app.
Text in the results bar no longer wraps or gets clipped when it is enlarged.
The results bar no longer floats above the bottom edge, and inputs no longer hide behind it.

v0_2_0.notes:
Renamed the app to The Spoke Calculator and set its typeface to Sora.
The app now lives at /the-spoke-calculator/.
Wheel comparison can use your current inputs without saving them first.
Modals fade in and out, and the page behind them no longer scrolls.
Preset options wrap so they stay readable on a phone, and screen rotation follows the device setting.

v0_1_0.notes:
First release.
Spoke length calculation, with hub and rim presets to fill the form.
Saving and reloading results, plus JSON export and import.
Sharing the input conditions by URL, and comparing two wheels.
English and Japanese, with light and dark themes.
